correctness.rationale: With μ,D,r>0 and X_0~N(0,D/μ), ordinary OU and resetting to a uniformly selected past time preserve the same Gaussian one-time law, but not temporal stationarity. Set A_t=∫_0^t X_u du, y=E[A_t²], c=E[X_t A_t], v=D/μ, b=μ+r: generator and history averaging give y'=2c and c'=v−bc+(r/t)y, hence y''+by'−2r y/t=2v. Conditions y(0)=y'(0)=0 and 0≤y≤vt² establish Laplace transform Y(s)=2v/[b(p−1)s²]((1+b/s)^(p−1)−1), p=2r/b; invert to confluent hypergeometric variance formula, taking a logarithmic limit at p=1. Negative-real-axis Kummer asymptotics and the critical integral yield the exact T^−1, T^−1 logT, and T^(p−2) coefficients for r<μ, =μ, >μ. All tend to zero for finite r. Independently differentiated the exact function numerically for four parameter regimes with high precision and checked ODE residual; this corroborates but does not prove the L² limit or the asymptotic.

value.rationale: A natural finite-time and long-time statistical efficiency question is not determined by identical equilibrium one-time Gaussians for a non-Markovian memory-reset trajectory. The sharp r=μ transition and logarithmic boundary with leading constants distinguish ordinary inverse-time averaging from slow memory-driven decay, with no unsupported central limit or almost-sure claim.

limitations: All formulas unconditional and require stationary Gaussian initialization, positive OU confinement and resetting uniformly to the entire path history.
No assertion of temporal stationarity, central limit theorem or almost-sure ergodic rate.
